paper.title_en: Three-body model study of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math> using the Faddeev method in momentum space
paper.abstract_en: We employ the three-body model to the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus by solving the Faddeev equations in momentum space using the partial-wave decomposition method. Four sets of interactions between the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math> core and the neutron, <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></math>, are constructed in different ways to test the validity of the three-body model. The spectra of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math> are obtained, including the <math><msubsup><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math>, and <math><msubsup><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> states, together with the rms radii, <math><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></math>. Our results are consistent with previous three-body computations of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></math> in coordinate space and the most recent ab initio calculations. For the <math><msubsup><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math> ground state, the energies and radii of four sets of <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></math> are close to the experimental data. In particular, when <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></math> is constructed close to the realistic core-neutron interaction, the resulting probabilities of the <math><mi>p</mi></math>-wave configurations are similar to those obtained from earlier shell-model calculations. Additionally, we predict two excited states, <math><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> and <math><msubsup><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup></math>, together with their two-neutron separation energies. For the first excited <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></math> state, our calculations suggest that, if the <math><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> orbitals share the 1.28 MeV resonance state in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>11</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, then the three-body model could produce results that align with the experimental data.
